reviewPolicy: Concise paraphrases of linked wiki sources; area groupings follow the project's search taxonomy rather than official boundaries.

records.name: Richmond & Presidio
records.shortDescription: Parks across the Richmond District and Presidio edge.
records.overview: This project area spans the Richmond District and neighborhoods adjoining the Presidio in northwestern San Francisco. Its park choices range from small neighborhood spaces to coastal and historic landscapes.

records.name: Marina & North Beach
records.shortDescription: Waterfront, hillside, and neighborhood parks in northern San Francisco.
records.overview: This project area follows San Francisco's northern waterfront and nearby hills, connecting the Marina, North Beach, Russian Hill, and adjoining neighborhoods. The grouping is intended to make nearby park options easier to browse.

records.name: Downtown, Chinatown & SoMa
records.shortDescription: Dense downtown neighborhoods with plazas, playgrounds, and waterfront spaces.
records.overview: This project area brings together central and eastern neighborhoods around Downtown, Chinatown, and South of Market. Parks here often serve dense residential, commercial, and visitor districts.

sources.title: South of Market, San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Haight, Castro & Central
records.shortDescription: Hilltop, residential, and cultural neighborhoods near the city center.
records.overview: This project area connects central San Francisco neighborhoods around the Haight, Castro, Twin Peaks, and Western Addition. The terrain and neighborhood character vary considerably across the grouping.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Sunset & Westside
records.shortDescription: Westside parks stretching from inland hills toward the Pacific.
records.overview: This project area covers much of western San Francisco, including the Sunset District, Lakeshore, and neighborhoods around Golden Gate Park. Large landscapes and smaller recreation sites both appear in this grouping.

records.name: Mission, Bernal & Noe
records.shortDescription: Parks across central-southern valleys, hills, and residential neighborhoods.
records.overview: This project area groups the Mission with Bernal Heights, Noe Valley, Glen Park, and nearby southern neighborhoods. Its park network includes civic gathering places, hilltop open spaces, and neighborhood recreation sites.

records.name: Southeast San Francisco
records.shortDescription: Bay shoreline, hill, and neighborhood parks across southeastern San Francisco.
records.overview: This project area extends through southeastern San Francisco from Potrero Hill and Mission Bay to Bayview–Hunters Point and Visitacion Valley. Its parks reflect shoreline, industrial, residential, and hill landscapes.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Treasure Island
records.shortDescription: Parks on Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island in San Francisco Bay.
records.overview: This project area covers park destinations associated with Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island in San Francisco Bay. The islands combine developed areas, shoreline settings, and broad views of the region.

records.name: Outside San Francisco
records.shortDescription: San Francisco recreation properties located beyond the city boundary.
records.overview: San Francisco Recreation and Parks manages a small number of destinations outside San Francisco. This project grouping keeps those properties discoverable without treating them as city neighborhoods.

records.name: Bayview Hunters Point
records.shortDescription: Southeastern waterfront neighborhoods shaped by industry and community life.
records.overview: Bayview–Hunters Point occupies southeastern San Francisco along the bay. Its history includes maritime industry, working-class communities, environmental advocacy, and continuing neighborhood change.

records.name: Bernal Heights
records.shortDescription: A residential hill neighborhood between the Mission and southeastern districts.
records.overview: Bernal Heights is centered on a prominent hill south of the Mission District. Parks and open spaces take advantage of its slopes, ridgeline, and residential setting.

records.name: Castro/Upper Market
records.shortDescription: Central neighborhoods known for LGBTQ+ history, hills, and active streets.
records.overview: The Castro and Upper Market occupy a central valley and surrounding slopes. The Castro is internationally associated with San Francisco's LGBTQ+ history and community life.

records.name: Chinatown
records.shortDescription: A dense historic neighborhood in central San Francisco.
records.overview: San Francisco's Chinatown is one of North America's oldest and best-known Chinese enclaves. Its dense blocks include civic spaces and parks serving residents and visitors.

records.name: Excelsior
records.shortDescription: A diverse southern neighborhood organized around Mission Street.
records.overview: The Excelsior is a southern San Francisco neighborhood extending toward the county line. Mission Street is a principal corridor through its residential and commercial landscape.

records.name: Financial District/South Beach
records.shortDescription: Downtown blocks and an eastern waterfront neighborhood beside the bay.
records.overview: This filter combines the Financial District's commercial core with South Beach along San Francisco's eastern waterfront. Public spaces range from compact plazas to shoreline parks.

records.name: Glen Park
records.shortDescription: A southern neighborhood beside Glen Canyon's steep natural landscape.
records.overview: Glen Park is a residential neighborhood adjoining Glen Canyon in south-central San Francisco. The canyon gives the area an unusually rugged open-space corridor.

records.name: Golden Gate Park
records.shortDescription: San Francisco's large westside park and its many destinations.
records.overview: Golden Gate Park stretches west from central San Francisco toward the Pacific Ocean. The filter groups the park's many gardens, recreation spaces, cultural institutions, and landscapes.

records.name: Haight Ashbury
records.shortDescription: A central neighborhood closely associated with 1960s counterculture.
records.overview: Haight-Ashbury sits east of Golden Gate Park beneath the central hills. It is widely known for its role in the counterculture of the 1960s.

records.name: Hayes Valley
records.shortDescription: A central neighborhood of residential streets and active commercial blocks.
records.overview: Hayes Valley is a central San Francisco neighborhood west of Civic Center. Changes to the former freeway corridor reshaped its streets and public spaces.

records.name: Inner Richmond
records.shortDescription: The eastern Richmond District between the Presidio and Golden Gate Park.
records.overview: Inner Richmond forms the eastern portion of the Richmond District, between the Presidio and Golden Gate Park. Its parks connect residential streets with larger landscapes nearby.

records.name: Inner Sunset
records.shortDescription: A westside neighborhood beside Golden Gate Park and Mount Sutro.
records.overview: Inner Sunset lies south of Golden Gate Park near Mount Sutro. Its parks serve residential and commercial areas while connecting to larger westside landscapes.

records.name: Japantown
records.shortDescription: A historic Japanese American cultural district in central San Francisco.
records.overview: San Francisco's Japantown is one of the few remaining historic Japantowns in the United States. Its public spaces sit within a compact cultural and commercial district.

records.name: Lakeshore
records.shortDescription: A southwestern area near Lake Merced and the Pacific coast.
records.overview: Lakeshore occupies southwestern San Francisco around Lake Merced and nearby residential districts. Water, open space, and recreation facilities shape many local park experiences.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Lincoln Park
records.shortDescription: Coastal parkland at San Francisco's northwestern edge.
records.overview: Lincoln Park occupies coastal terrain in northwestern San Francisco near Lands End. The area combines recreation, wooded slopes, and views toward the Golden Gate.

records.name: Lone Mountain/USF
records.shortDescription: A hilltop district centered on Lone Mountain and the USF campus.
records.overview: Lone Mountain rises between the Richmond District and Western Addition. The University of San Francisco campus is a defining presence in the area.

records.name: Marina
records.shortDescription: A northern waterfront neighborhood beside the Presidio and bay.
records.overview: The Marina District occupies San Francisco's northern waterfront between Fort Mason and the Presidio. Much of the neighborhood was developed on former bay shoreline and fill.

records.name: McLaren Park
records.shortDescription: A large hill park serving southeastern San Francisco neighborhoods.
records.overview: John McLaren Park is one of San Francisco's largest parks, occupying hills in the city's southeast. It contains varied recreation areas, paths, and open landscapes.

records.name: Mission
records.shortDescription: A central neighborhood with deep Latino heritage and active public spaces.
records.overview: The Mission District grew around Mission San Francisco de Asís and became a major center of Latino culture in San Francisco. Its parks support dense residential and commercial streets.

records.name: Mission Bay
records.shortDescription: A newer eastern waterfront neighborhood built around Mission Creek.
records.overview: Mission Bay is an eastern waterfront neighborhood developed from former rail yards and industrial land. New housing, institutions, and parks line Mission Creek and the bay edge.

records.name: Nob Hill
records.shortDescription: A steep central hill neighborhood above Downtown and Chinatown.
records.overview: Nob Hill rises above Downtown and Chinatown in central San Francisco. Its steep streets, historic hotels, and dense residential blocks shape its public spaces.

records.name: Noe Valley
records.shortDescription: A residential valley and hillside neighborhood in central San Francisco.
records.overview: Noe Valley lies between the Castro, Mission, and southern hills. It developed largely in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries and includes many Victorian and Edwardian homes.

records.name: North Beach
records.shortDescription: A historic northern neighborhood associated with Italian heritage and the Beats.
records.overview: North Beach sits between Chinatown and the northern waterfront. The neighborhood is associated with Italian American history, cafés, and the Beat literary movement.

records.name: Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside
records.shortDescription: Southwestern neighborhoods connected by Ocean Avenue and nearby transit.
records.overview: Oceanview, Merced Heights, and Ingleside form a group of residential neighborhoods in southwestern San Francisco. Ocean Avenue, City College, and nearby rail lines connect the area.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Outer Mission
records.shortDescription: A southern neighborhood along Mission Street near the county line.
records.overview: Outer Mission lies along Mission Street in southern San Francisco. Residential streets and neighborhood parks extend toward the city's border with Daly City.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Outer Richmond
records.shortDescription: The western Richmond District between Golden Gate Park and the Presidio.
records.overview: Outer Richmond extends toward the Pacific Ocean between Golden Gate Park and the Presidio. Coastal weather and proximity to large open spaces shape the neighborhood.

records.name: Pacific Heights
records.shortDescription: A northern hill neighborhood known for historic homes and bay views.
records.overview: Pacific Heights occupies elevated ground south of the Marina. The neighborhood is known for historic residences, steep streets, and views toward San Francisco Bay.

records.name: Portola
records.shortDescription: A southeastern hill neighborhood above Bayview and Visitacion Valley.
records.overview: Portola occupies hills in southeastern San Francisco between Bernal Heights, Bayview, and Visitacion Valley. Residential streets climb toward open spaces and broad views.

records.name: Potrero Hill
records.shortDescription: A sunny eastern hill neighborhood overlooking the bay and Downtown.
records.overview: Potrero Hill rises above San Francisco's eastern waterfront. Its slopes offer views toward Downtown and the bay, with parks embedded throughout residential blocks.

records.name: Presidio
records.shortDescription: A former military post now managed as part of a national park.
records.overview: The Presidio is a former military post at the Golden Gate, now part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area. Forests, historic buildings, shoreline, and recreation landscapes define the district.

records.name: Presidio Heights
records.shortDescription: A residential neighborhood along the Presidio's southern edge.
records.overview: Presidio Heights lies immediately south of the Presidio between the Richmond District and Pacific Heights. Its parks serve a compact residential area beside larger federal parkland.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Russian Hill
records.shortDescription: A steep northern hill neighborhood between the waterfront and Downtown.
records.overview: Russian Hill rises above the northern waterfront between North Beach and the Marina. Its steep slopes, stairways, and views strongly shape local parks and streets.

records.name: Seacliff
records.shortDescription: A small coastal neighborhood overlooking the Golden Gate.
records.overview: Sea Cliff occupies coastal bluffs in northwestern San Francisco between the Presidio and Lands End. Its setting provides access to shoreline landscapes and Golden Gate views.

records.name: South of Market
records.shortDescription: A large central district shaped by industry, redevelopment, and major institutions.
records.overview: South of Market, commonly called SoMa, covers a broad area south of Market Street. Warehouses, housing, cultural institutions, and redevelopment coexist across its varied subdistricts.

sources.title: South of Market, San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Sunset/Parkside
records.shortDescription: Broad westside neighborhoods extending toward Ocean Beach.
records.overview: The Sunset and Parkside occupy much of western San Francisco between Golden Gate Park and the city's southern neighborhoods. Their grid of residential streets extends toward the Pacific coast.

records.name: Tenderloin
records.shortDescription: A dense central neighborhood with a long residential and cultural history.
records.overview: The Tenderloin is a dense central neighborhood west of Union Square and north of Market Street. Its residential hotels, cultural institutions, and community organizations reflect a complex urban history.

records.name: Treasure Island
records.shortDescription: A human-made bay island paired with the natural Yerba Buena Island.
records.overview: Treasure Island was created in San Francisco Bay in the twentieth century and is connected to Yerba Buena Island. Parks and shoreline spaces offer expansive regional views.

records.name: Twin Peaks
records.shortDescription: Central hills with some of San Francisco's broadest views.
records.overview: Twin Peaks are prominent hills near the geographic center of San Francisco. The surrounding open space is known for exposed slopes, habitat, and panoramic views.

records.name: Visitacion Valley
records.shortDescription: A southeastern valley neighborhood near the San Francisco county line.
records.overview: Visitacion Valley lies in southeastern San Francisco near the county boundary. Hills surround its residential streets and neighborhood commercial corridor.

records.name: West of Twin Peaks
records.shortDescription: Residential neighborhoods on the western slopes of San Francisco's central hills.
records.overview: West of Twin Peaks is a broad planning and geographic term for neighborhoods beyond the city's central hills. The area's parks occupy residential valleys, slopes, and ridgelines.

sources.title: List of neighborhoods in San Francisco — Wikipedia

records.name: Western Addition
records.shortDescription: A central district encompassing historic residential and cultural neighborhoods.
records.overview: The Western Addition lies west of central San Francisco and includes several smaller neighborhoods. Its history includes Victorian development, Japanese American and African American communities, and disruptive urban renewal.
